name: Zoom

steps.d: In the Zoom App Marketplace, click Developer, then Develop and Build an app. Select General app and click Create.
Enter your redirect URL and add it to the OAuth allow lists. Both are required.
On the Scopes page, add only the scopes you need and explain why each is needed.
On the Local Test page, select Add App Now and then Allow.
Other accounts can install the app after it passes Zoom's App Submission Review.

Public apps go through a Marketplace review and a security audit before external users can install them.

checklist.answer: In the Zoom App Marketplace, click Developer, then Develop and Build an app. Select General app and click Create.
Apps can be admin-managed, added by account admins, or user-managed, added by individual users. A separate server-to-server OAuth app type also exists.
The OAuth redirect URL and the OAuth allow lists are required. Strict Mode URL and the subdomain check are optional.
Strict Mode allows only redirects that exactly match your OAuth redirect URLs. The subdomain check allows only redirects that match the subdomain exactly.
Zoom generates a client ID and client secret for your app. Development and production credentials differ, so use the production ones when you publish.
Add scopes on the Scopes page and explain why each is needed. Adding one is a request to the Zoom Security Review team, which may reject a scope you don't need.
All public apps must pass Zoom's App Submission Review for security, functionality and information. Apps for users in your own account don't need the standard Marketplace review.
Beta apps are for testing. They can be shared only with members of your own Zoom account, and they can't be published to the Marketplace.
Apps can be rejected if the long description lacks detail about features and functionality. Even unlisted apps still need listing details such as images and descriptions.
